question: What does patient harm mean specifically in reproductive health?

options.A: Unintended injury during pregnancy, childbirth, and women's care
options.B: Nutritional issues found during child checkups
options.C: Drug side effects in elderly male patients
options.D: Surgical issues linked to bone and joint procedures

explanation: Reproductive health harm specifically involves issues that happen during maternal, newborn, and gynecological care. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h1)

question: A patient gets an obstetric fistula after a long, blocked labor. How is this classified?

options.A: A minor side effect from anesthesia
options.C: Preventable physical harm linked to how care was given
options.D: A normal body change during pregnancy

explanation: Obstetric fistula often happens when labor care is delayed or inadequate, which counts as preventable physical harm. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h1)

question: What do you call an error that is caught before it ever reaches the patient?
explanation: A near miss is a close call where an unsafe action is stopped before it can harm a patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h2)

question: A surgical sponge is left inside a patient during a C-section. What is this called?
explanation: Leaving items behind in surgery is a serious, highly preventable mistake known as a never event. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why do safety experts focus on fixing system flaws instead of just blaming staff?

options.A: Nurses cannot be sued for medical mistakes
options.B: Hospital bosses prefer to ignore human errors
options.C: Staff members never make mistakes on duty
options.D: Errors usually happen because workplace processes are broken

explanation: Issues like bad communication and poor staffing create environments where human error is much more likely to occur. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h3)

question: Leaving out a key detail about a postpartum patient's bleeding during shift handover is an example of what?
explanation: Failing to pass on complete patient details during shift changes is a failure in communication between healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which sign shows early postpartum hemorrhage and needs quick checking?

options.A: Warm, dry skin with high oxygen levels
options.B: A slow, steady resting heart rate of 50 beats per minute
options.C: High urine output above normal limits
options.D: Fast heart rate and dropping blood pressure

explanation: When blood loss starts, the body tries to compensate by increasing the heart rate before blood pressure drops sharply. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses to stay alert and keep watching patients closely?

options.A: To get an automatic promotion to senior management
options.B: To reduce hospital electricity use at night
options.C: To catch early signs that a patient is getting worse
options.D: To get rid of all paperwork in the ward

explanation: Regular checks help nurses spot small changes in vital signs before emergencies get out of hand. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the nurse's very first priority when a severe adverse event happens?

options.A: Writing a long incident report for the hospital lawyer
options.B: Stabilizing the patient and calling for emergency help
options.C: Leaving the bedside to look for missing tools
options.D: Calling the media about the care failure

explanation: Patient safety and emergency care always come first when an unexpected crisis happens. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h5)

question: How should a nurse talk to a patient and family after an unexpected medical error?

options.A: By blaming other departments to avoid trouble
options.B: By using big medical words to confuse the family
options.C: By avoiding them and refusing to talk

explanation: Being open and compassionate helps maintain trust and supports families through difficult situations. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason for filling out an incident report after a safety event?

options.A: To add more paperwork to the day
options.B: To find weak spots in the system and stop future errors
options.C: To hide mistakes from insurance auditors
options.D: To find an easy reason to fire staff

explanation: Incident reports help hospitals improve by showing where workflows and systems need fixing. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h6)

question: Why does a work culture based on punishment fail to improve patient safety?

options.A: It speeds up patient discharges too much
options.B: It makes nurses report every tiny delay
options.C: It makes staff hide mistakes out of fear
options.D: It forces hospitals to buy expensive gear

explanation: When workers are afraid of being punished, they keep quiet about near misses, stopping the hospital from learning. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h6)

question: A maternity ward wants to cut down on bleeding-related injuries. Which action helps most?

options.A: Taking part in regular emergency simulation drills with the whole team
options.B: Stopping all vital sign checks right after delivery
options.C: Relying only on patient memory to track blood loss
options.D: Waiting for a maternal death review before changing anything

explanation: Simulations help the team practice working together so they can handle high-risk emergencies smoothly. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent patient harm?

options.A: Communicating well with the healthcare team
options.B: Ignoring hospital safety checklists during busy shifts
options.C: Taking part in quality improvement projects

explanation: Skipping safety checklists raises the chance of missing important steps and harming patients. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h7)
